suggestions.assertion: All workers are spawned in a single message (single Task tool invocation batch) — NOT spawned sequentially one at a time
suggestions.reason: The assertion cannot distinguish between a run that skipped worker agents entirely (as happened here) and one that correctly used a single batch of Task invocations. A self-reported transcript saying 'simulated as parallel research streams' technically satisfies the surface reading. The assertion should explicitly require evidence of Task tool calls in the transcript, not just a claim of parallelism.

suggestions.assertion: Spawns 2-3 workers — one per comparison dimension (PostgreSQL, MySQL, benchmarks/cases)
suggestions.reason: Same issue as above. The count of '3 workers' is self-reported by the executor as a simulation label. Without verifying actual Task tool calls in the transcript, this assertion can be trivially satisfied by labeling any research approach as '3 workers.' Consider requiring: 'Transcript shows 2-3 Task tool invocations in the same message.'

No assertion checks whether the citation-analyst sub-agent was invoked to verify source quality. The skill has an explicit step for this, and it was skipped. A failing citation-analyst step could result in stale, broken, or inaccurate citations — a significant quality gap uncovered by the current eval set.

The bibliography expectation checks for source count and recency but not whether URLs are live/accessible. The transcript documents 4 fetch failures (404, 500, SSL, empty). Source [12] (Percona) is listed in the bibliography but the transcript notes it returned 'limited content.' An assertion checking citation quality (e.g., each cited source was successfully fetched) would be more discriminating.

eval_feedback.overall: The report content quality is genuinely good — balanced, well-cited, with real contradictions identified. The main gap is that the two most important process assertions (worker spawning) cannot be verified from the transcript because the skill's sub-agent mechanism was bypassed. The eval set would benefit from at least one assertion that requires observable Task tool evidence, making it impossible to pass by simulation.
